examples.scenario: Inverse geotransform is assumed valid without checking inversion success.
examples.reason: GDAL exposes explicit inverse failure; target pixel addressing cannot continue when the affine transform is uninvertible.

examples.scenario: The first pixel center is treated as pixel coordinate (0,0).
examples.reason: GDAL defines (0,0) as the upper-left corner and (0.5,0.5) as the first pixel center.

examples.scenario: North-up Y indexing ignores that GT(5) is negative.
examples.reason: North-up rasters normally decrease georeferenced Y as line index increases.

examples.scenario: A negative fractional inverse pixel coordinate is cast to int toward zero.
examples.reason: Truncation and floor differ for negative values and can turn an outside coordinate into pixel zero.

examples.scenario: A coordinate exactly on a grid edge is assigned after seeing which side has a nicer elevation.
examples.reason: Left/right or half-open edge ownership must be defined before numeric values are inspected.

examples.scenario: nextafter is used to move a parcel coordinate just inside a cell and that moved coordinate becomes canonical.
examples.reason: One-ULP probes are QA diagnostics only; they cannot mutate authoritative geometry.

examples.scenario: A floating-point RasterIO window is used for terminal sampling.
examples.reason: Floating windows can invoke resampling semantics; terminal evidence should use exact integer native-cell windows.

examples.scenario: Read buffer size is smaller than the source window and GDAL decimates automatically.
examples.reason: Different source and buffer sizes can resample and may select an overview.

examples.scenario: A window extends one cell outside the raster and the returned fill value is included as terrain.
examples.reason: Out-of-range requests must fail closed rather than turn zero/nodata fill into a height candidate.

examples.scenario: projwin behavior is assumed identical across GDAL versions.
examples.reason: GDAL 3.11 changed how projwin extents are transformed and selected.

examples.scenario: Nearest-neighbor projwin expands to pixel boundaries and the expanded cells are treated as parcel members.
examples.reason: Extraction-window rounding is not equivalent to exact parcel membership.

examples.scenario: Row/column is flattened with Fortran order in one replay and C order in another.
examples.reason: The same row/column maps to different flat indices under C and F order.

examples.scenario: ravel_multi_index(mode='wrap') converts column -1 to the last column.
examples.reason: Out-of-range target indices must raise, not wrap into valid-looking cells.

examples.scenario: ravel_multi_index(mode='clip') converts an out-of-range index to an edge cell.
examples.reason: Clipping can fabricate an edge-cell sample that was never addressed by the source coordinate.

examples.scenario: Flat index is stored without raster width/height and order metadata.
examples.reason: Flat-index identity depends on shape and linearization order.

examples.scenario: ravel then unravel returns a different row/column pair.
examples.reason: Linear-index serialization must round-trip exactly before it can identify a raster cell.

examples.scenario: Coordinate-to-pixel-to-coordinate round trip differs materially but sampling continues.
examples.reason: The addressing transform must be reproducible and any unexplained drift blocks terminal sampling.

examples.scenario: A pixel exactly at raster width is treated as the final valid column.
examples.reason: Valid columns are 0 through width-1; the right boundary itself is outside a half-open raster index interval.

examples.scenario: A pixel exactly at raster height is treated as the final valid row.
examples.reason: Valid rows are 0 through height-1; the bottom boundary is outside the index domain.

examples.scenario: searchsorted side='left' changes to side='right' during refactor.
examples.reason: Exact-boundary ownership changes when left/right insertion semantics change.

examples.scenario: digitize returns a bin index outside range and code indexes without checking.
examples.reason: Out-of-range grid coordinates need explicit bounds checks before array indexing.

examples.scenario: Rotation coefficients are assumed zero without reading them.
examples.reason: All six coefficients are part of addressing; non-zero rotation changes inverse mapping.

examples.scenario: The inverse transform succeeds but source/target axis order is wrong.
examples.reason: Successful math does not prove coordinates were supplied in the correct CRS axis convention.

examples.scenario: Window equality is checked only by pixel count, not exact index set.
examples.reason: Equal counts can still represent different raster cells.

examples.scenario: Independent addressing replay selects the same extrema value from a different pixel.
examples.reason: Numeric agreement does not replace exact cell-identity agreement.

examples.scenario: A partially outside parcel is sampled only over the in-raster portion and called complete.
examples.reason: Final extrema require complete authoritative parcel coverage or an explicit no-data state.

examples.scenario: Coordinate addressing QA completes while canonical point rows remain zero.
examples.reason: Addressing guards can advance without inventing target coordinates or elevations.

examples.scenario: Missing ACK is bypassed by starting a second coordinate-sampling runner.
examples.reason: The continuation contract requires the existing single shared runner.

examples.scenario: The four known execution blockers are relabeled pending.
examples.reason: Known unresolved conditions remain blocked; pending stays zero.

examples.scenario: Batch 71 is reported as a measured parcel height result.
examples.reason: Real output still requires canonical points, exact boundary/raster binding, execution, numeric sampling and readback.
